answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can use earned-history gating: every identity starts with near-zero trust, and the right to transact grows only over a long horizon of verified, useful work. Newcomers sprout like yarrow in a grove — cheap to plant, but each must prove itself over time before it can move real value. An attacker can mint thousands of identities, yet each still faces the same slow climb, so flooding the network costs months of genuine effort per fake while honest agents keep their accumulated standing.
